name: security-android-fileprovider-grants-review
intent: FileProvider root selection and temporary URI permission scope
artifacts: Provider paths/exports, grant flags, share intent targets and actual file open logic.
trace: Trace which app receives which URI and whether it can access files beyond the intended shared object through path/root or grant handling.
experiment: Use owned emulator apps and synthetic files inside/outside a share root; compare intended URI access and one unauthorized file request.
disproof: A content URI or broad-looking path XML is not arbitrary file access without an effective granted/open path.
repair: Constrain roots and URI grants, then retest legitimate shares, grant lifetime and outside-file denial.
branch_decisions: Trace configured roots, canonical path resolution, manifest export/grant settings and individual Intent/ClipData grants. A broad root is potential reach, not proof an attacker has a usable URI grant. Separate read from write and persisted versus temporary access; use owned marker files and verify the effective recipient operation and grant revocation.
operational_method: Record provider root mapping, canonical file, actual recipient and grant flags on Intent/ClipData, including prefix scope where supported. Separate read/write and actual supported persistability; a client requesting persistence does not make every provider grant persistable. Compare a marker URI with a sibling/outside-root URI and observe permissions after the documented temporary-grant lifetime/revocation event. Exported=false alone does not invalidate an explicitly issued grant.
